title: Unit-character twist and coefficient extension on monomial ideal tensors
statement:
Let $Q$ be a commutative monoid written additively, $K\subset Q$ a monoid ideal ($K+Q\subset K$, allowing $\varnothing$), $A$ a commutative ring, and $b:Q\to(A,\cdot)$ and $u:Q\to A^\times$ homomorphisms. Put $c(q)=u(q)b(q)$. For any commutative ring $D$, $D[Q]$ is the ring of finite sums $\sum d_qz^q$ with $z^qz^p=z^{q+p}$ and $D[K]$ is the ideal spanned by $z^k$, $k\in K$. For $d=b,c$, let $A_d$ be $A$ with the $\mathbf Z[Q]$ action $z^q\mapsto d(q)$ and with the $A[Q]$ action $a_0z^q\mapsto a_0d(q)$ as appropriate.
There is an $A$-linear isomorphism of module tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]
$$\rho:\mathbf Z[K]\otimes_{\mathbf Z[Q]}A_c\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf Z[K]\otimes_{\mathbf Z[Q]}A_b,\qquad z^q\otimes a\longmapsto z^q\otimes u(q)a,$$
with inverse $z^q\otimes a\mapsto z^q\otimes u(q)^{-1}a$. For $d=b,c$, the coefficient map
$$\iota_d:\mathbf Z[K]\otimes_{\mathbf Z[Q]}A_d\xrightarrow{\sim}A[K]\otimes_{A[Q]}A_d,\qquad z^q\otimes a\longmapsto z^q\otimes a$$
is an $A$-linear isomorphism with inverse $(a_0z^q)\otimes a\mapsto z^q\otimes a_0a$. Let $\tau_u:A[Q]\to A[Q]$ be the $A$-algebra automorphism $z^q\mapsto u(q)z^q$. It preserves $A[K]$ and the evaluation homomorphisms satisfy $\operatorname{ev}_c=\operatorname{ev}_b\tau_u$. In the coefficient-extended presentations, $\rho$ is exactly the ideal-tensor map induced by $\tau_u$ and the identity on $A$. All displayed isomorphisms commute with the multiplication maps to $A$ and with the identity on that target, and are natural under coefficient homomorphisms carrying $b,u$ to the chosen new characters. No flatness over $\mathbf Z$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write $R=\mathbf Z[Q]$, $I=\mathbf Z[K]$ and $T_d=I\otimes_R A_d$. Every element of $I$ has a unique finite expression $\sum_{k\in K}n_kz^k$: multiplication by $z^p$ preserves this support because $K+Q\subset K$. By the quotient construction of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], $T_d$ has the following presentation as an $A$-module: generators $e_k=z^k\otimes1$ for $k\in K$ and relations $e_{k+p}=d(p)e_k$ for $k\in K,p\in Q$. Indeed, let $E_d$ be the free $A$-module on $K$ modulo these relations. The formula $(\sum n_kz^k,a)\mapsto\sum n_kae_k$ is biadditive and $R$-balanced, since for each monomial $z^p$ its two values are $\sum n_kae_{k+p}$ and $\sum n_kd(p)ae_k$. Finite sums give balancing for every element of $R$. It therefore induces an additive map $T_d\to E_d$ by the defining quotient; it is $A$-linear for the action on the second tensor factor. Conversely $e_k\mapsto z^k\otimes1$ respects the relations by balancing in $T_d$. These maps are inverse on $e_k$ and on every $z^k\otimes a$, which generate the respective modules. This proves the presentation without an exactness or flatness theorem.

proof.text: The coefficient-extended tensor $U_d=A[K]\otimes_{A[Q]}A_d$ has the identical $A$-module presentation. In fact $(\sum a_kz^k,a)\mapsto\sum a_kae_k$ is $A$-bilinear and balanced: for a scalar monomial $rz^p$ the required equation is $\sum ra_kae_{k+p}=\sum a_krd(p)ae_k$, exactly the defining relation of $E_d$. By [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] it descends to $U_d\to E_d$, inverse to $e_k\mapsto z^k\otimes1$. Thus the identity on $E_d$ gives $\iota_d:T_d\simeq U_d$. On generators it is $z^k\otimes a\mapsto z^k\otimes a$; its inverse sends $(a_0z^k)\otimes a$ to $z^k\otimes a_0a$, using balancing by the constant $a_0$. This constructs both coefficient isomorphisms for $d=b,c$.

proof.text: Use the presentations just proved to define $\rho(e_k^c)=u(k)e_k^b$ $A$-linearly. It respects every relation, because $u(k+p)e_{k+p}^b=u(k)u(p)b(p)e_k^b=c(p)u(k)e_k^b$. Define the reverse map by $e_k^b\mapsto u(k)^{-1}e_k^c$; here $u(k+p)^{-1}e_{k+p}^c=u(k)^{-1}u(p)^{-1}c(p)e_k^c=b(p)u(k)^{-1}e_k^c$. Each composite is the identity on every generator, since $u(k)$ is a unit. The generation clause of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] now gives mutually inverse $A$-linear maps, with exactly the stated formulas for $z^k\otimes a$.

source.place: Tags 00CV (algebra-section-tensor-product), 00CW (algebra-definition-bilinear), 00CX (algebra-lemma-tensor-product), quotient construction in the proof; explicit monomial calculations by the worker.

proof.text: Define $\tau_u(\sum a_qz^q)=\sum a_qu(q)z^q$. It is additive, fixes constants since $u(0)=1$, and is multiplicative since the images of $z^qz^p$ and $z^q$ times the image of $z^p$ both equal $u(q)u(p)z^{q+p}$. Distributivity over finite sums proves this for arbitrary inputs. The identical construction with $u^{-1}$ is inverse. Both maps preserve support, hence preserve $A[K]$. For each monomial, $\operatorname{ev}_b\tau_u(a_qz^q)=a_qu(q)b(q)=a_qc(q)=\operatorname{ev}_c(a_qz^q)$; additivity proves the equality of evaluation homomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 00CV (algebra-section-tensor-product), 00CW (algebra-definition-bilinear), 00CX (algebra-lemma-tensor-product), quotient construction in the proof; explicit monomial calculations by the worker.

proof.text: The map on extended ideal tensors induced by $\tau_u$ and $1_A$ is $h_c\otimes a\mapsto\tau_u(h_c)\otimes a$. To check balancing for $r\in A[Q]$, compute $\tau_u(rh_c)\otimes a=\tau_u(h_c)\otimes\operatorname{ev}_b(\tau_u(r))a=\tau_u(h_c)\otimes\operatorname{ev}_c(r)a$. Additivity and $A$-linearity are immediate from the formulas, so the quotient construction of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives the map. On $z^k\otimes a$ its value is $u(k)z^k\otimes a=z^k\otimes u(k)a$. Hence it equals $\iota_b\rho\iota_c^{-1}$ on the generators, and therefore on the whole tensor.

source.place: Tags 00CV (algebra-section-tensor-product), 00CW (algebra-definition-bilinear), 00CX (algebra-lemma-tensor-product), quotient construction in the proof; explicit monomial calculations by the worker.

proof.text: For either presentation, the multiplication map $\mu_d$ sends $z^k\otimes a$ to $d(k)a$ (and $(a_0z^k)\otimes a$ to $a_0d(k)a$). It is defined on the quotient because evaluation is multiplicative. Then $\mu_b\rho(z^k\otimes a)=b(k)u(k)a=c(k)a=\mu_c(z^k\otimes a)$, and $\mu_d\iota_d(z^k\otimes a)=d(k)a$. By the generation clause of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] these equalities prove all multiplication squares, with $1_A$ on their targets. The inverse squares follow by composing with the inverse isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 00CV (algebra-section-tensor-product), 00CW (algebra-definition-bilinear), 00CX (algebra-lemma-tensor-product), quotient construction in the proof; explicit monomial calculations by the worker.

proof.text: Let $f:A\to A'$ be a unital coefficient homomorphism with $b'=f\circ b$ and $u'(q)=f(u(q))$ on units, so $c'=f\circ c$. On each tensor presentation the coefficient map is the additive, $f$-semilinear map $z^k\otimes a\mapsto z^k\otimes f(a)$, well defined since the presentation relation $e_{k+p}=d(p)e_k$ maps to $e'_{k+p}=f(d(p))e'_k$. The two paths in the $\rho$ square both send this generator to $z^k\otimes f(u(k))f(a)$. The $\iota_d$ squares both send it to $z^k\otimes f(a)$; for its inverse use $f(a_0a)=f(a_0)f(a)$. On a monomial the $\tau_u$ square reads $f(a_q)u'(q)z^q=f(a_qu(q))z^q$, and multiplication squares read $f(d(k)a)=f(d(k))f(a)$. Additivity and generation as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] prove naturality everywhere, including inverses since $f(u(k)^{-1})=f(u(k))^{-1}$. None of these constructions required $A$ or $A'$ to be flat over $\mathbf Z$.
